Don't show this message again Close Print Up to 3.8% in the EU Overview The euro area annual inflation rate was 3.8 % in September 2026 , up from 3.2% in August . A year earlier, the rate was 2.2 %. European Union annual inflation was 3.8 % in September 2026 , up from 3.2% in August . A year earlier, the rate was 2.6 %. These figures are published by Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union . The lowest annual rates were registered in Sweden (1.0%), Hungary and Denmark (both 2.1%) . The highest annual rates were recorded in Romania (6.5%), Lithuania (6.1%) and Bulgaria (5.6%) . Compared with August 2026 , annual inflation fell in one Member State, remained stable in three and rose in twenty-three . In September 2026 , energy (+1.71 percentage points, pp), services (+1.52 percentage points, pp), non-energy industrial goods (+0.29 percentage points, pp) and food, alcohol & tobacco (+0.25 percentage points, pp) contributed positively to the annual euro area inflation rate. The euro area flash estimate for September 2026 , published on 2 October 2026 , was 3.8 %. The next flash estimate of euro area inflation with data for October 2026 is scheduled for 4 November 2026 . Methods and definitions Annual inflation is the price change of consumer goods and services between the current month and the same month of the previous year. Monthly inflation is the price change between the current month and the previous month. A contribution shows how much of the annual inflation rate comes from a particular component of the HICP. The contributions are calculated according to a method which ensures their additivity (allowing for rounding). Geographical information Up to December 31, 2025, the euro area included Belgium, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Slovenia, Slovakia and Finland (EA20) . From 1 January 2026, the euro area also includes Bulgaria (EA21) . The European Union includes Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Hungary, Malta, the Netherlands, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Finland and Sweden (EU27 ). The aggregate data series published in this Euro indicator release refer to the evolving composition of the euro area and the European Union. Thus, Euro indicator data for months up to December 2025 represent EA20 series, while Euro indicator data for January 2026 onwards represent EA21 series. Changes in the composition of the euro area are incorporated using a chain index formula. Don't show this message again Close Print €25.2 bn deficit for EU Euro area The first estimates of euro area balance showed a €16.1 bn deficit in trade in goods with the rest of the world in August 2026, compared with a deficit of €1.7 bn in August 2025. The euro area exports of goods to the rest of the world in August 2026 were €227.7 billion, an increase of 9.9% compared with August 2025 (€207.2 bn). Imports from the rest of the world stood at €243.8 bn, a rise of 16.7% compared with August 2025 (€208.9 bn). In August 2026, the euro area recorded a trade deficit of €16.1 bn, compared with a surplus of €10.7 bn in July 2026 and a deficit of €1.7 bn in August 2025. The decline compared with the same month of previous year was driven mainly by machinery and vehicles, the balance of which fell from a surplus of €7.2 bn to a € 0.7 deficit in August 2026. The energy deficit also widened, increasing from €21.3 bn to €26.7 bn. In January to August 2026, the euro area recorded a deficit of €5.4 bn, compared with a surplus of €90.9 bn in January-August 2025. The euro area exports of goods to the rest of the world rose to €1 990.8 bn (an increase of 2.1% compared with January-August 2025), and imports rose to €1 996.2 bn (an increase of 7.3% compared with January-August 2025). Intra-euro area trade rose to €1 857.6 bn in January-August 2026, up by 5.4% compared with January-August 2025. Figures are provisional. For more details, see information on data . Methods and definitions Statistics on trade in goods are transmitted monthly by the Member States, in accordance with the standard set out in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1197. For each reference month, Member States must compile statistics covering their total extra- and intra-EU trade by using estimates, where necessary. These data are available within 40 days after the end of the reference month, enabling euro area and EU aggregates to be disseminated within around 46 days. Member States provide Eurostat with raw data, which are adjusted for calendar and seasonal effects by Eurostat. The European aggregates are computed with the indirect approach (by Member States) for total imports and exports, which guarantees additivity between the aggregate and its respective components. The estimation of seasonally adjusted data is based on the Tramo-Seats procedure, which is available in the software JDemetra+. Data are broken down by broad categories of products as defined by the one-digit codes of the Standard international trade classification (SITC). Geographical information Euro area (EA21): Belgium, Bulgaria, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Slovenia, Slovakia and Finland.
